When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10** (calm price action) vs VIX Spike tier **2/4** with **60%** probability, skew and backwardation active
Price is quiet while options traders pay up for protection near term. Trust the VIX Spike Detector for direction of risk, because options reprice before stocks do, but keep size moderate since the tier is only **2** of **4**.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **72** (STRONG BUY, capitulation) vs Risk-off bias with **5** signals aligned and Contraction regime at **70%** confidence
The contrarian read says sentiment is washed out while the regime read says conditions are still weakening. Trust the contrarian score for entries on a multi-week view, and trust the regime read for how much you commit now. Scale in rather than buying in one clip.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime State score **31** (STABLE, no regime shift) vs Divergence composite ELEVATED with mother jaws at **100**
The regime gauge sees no shift yet, but **51.2%** of tracked pairs are diverging from their usual behavior. Trust the divergence picture as the early warning, since regime scores confirm late.

Price action is calm at **1/10** on the Crash Index, but options, regime and cross-asset signals lean defensive.
Bull
The Crash Index sits at **1** of **10** and the contrarian score reads **72**, a capitulation setup that has historically rewarded buyers. The Dow is up **1.3%** over five days and the Swiss market is up **3.0%**, so money is still finding a home.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector is at tier **2** of **4** with a **60%** probability, and both skew and backwardation are active. Five risk-off signals line up, the macro regime reads Contraction at **70%** confidence, and the Nasdaq 100 is down **3.3%** in five days.
The tell: Watch whether VIX backwardation fades back to a normal curve or the spike tier climbs from **2** to **3**. The first confirms the contrarian buy. The second confirms the risk-off bias.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market looks calm on price and uneasy underneath. The Crash Index is 1 of 10, yet the VIX Spike Detector sits at tier 2 of 4 with a 60% probability, and the Nasdaq 100 has slipped 3.3% in five days while the Dow gained 1.3%. That split says leadership is rotating away from growth, and the options market is already charging for it.

For positioning, you have a conflict between two good signals. The contrarian score of 72 flags capitulation, which argues for building long exposure. The regime read argues for patience: Contraction at 70% confidence, a regime score of 31, and 5 risk-off signals aligned. Start with partial size, favor the Dow-style leadership that is holding up, and keep room to add if volatility cools. Avoid heavy exposure to the growth complex while the Nasdaq 100 is the laggard.

The main risk is a jump in the VIX spike tier from 2 to 3 while backwardation stays active. That would turn a quiet pullback into a volatility event, and the Crash Index would catch up only after the damage. A fade in backwardation with the Nasdaq 100 stabilizing would flip the stance toward the contrarian buy.

A jump in the regime score well above 31 would signal that the slow cooling has become a break.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together have started to move apart. Correlation drift measures how much that link has changed, for example from +0.71 to -0.32.

The composite zone is ELEVATED, with 51.2% of the 43 pairs diverging, 14 bearish and 8 bullish for a net bias of 6 toward the bearish side. The mother jaws score is 100.

The sharpest breaks include stocks versus long bonds (+0.71 to -0.32), regional banks versus financials (+0.32 to -0.71), and Visa versus Mastercard (+0.84 to -0.66). High-beta versus low-volatility stocks loosened from +0.94 to +0.39.

Speculative growth versus the S&P 500 moved from -0.13 to +0.54, and the 10-year versus 2-year spread flipped from -0.40 to +0.41. When this many familiar relationships break at once, the market is repricing something, and the bearish lean says the repricing has a defensive tilt.

A fall in the share of diverging pairs would be the sign that things are settling.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is scattered, and the US session opens with a split. In Asia, Australia leads at +0.5% while Japan's Nikkei lags at -4.6%, a sharp drop that points to risk reduction in the region's growth-heavy and yen-sensitive markets.

Europe is firmer, with Switzerland at +3.0% and the FTSE at +0.3%, which fits a defensive rotation. In the US, the Dow leads at +1.3% while the Nasdaq 100 lags at -3.3%.

Crypto is flat, with Solana at +0.1% and Ether at -0.8%, so there is no extra risk appetite from the 24/7 market. The lead-lag says defensive and value-oriented stocks are favored and tech faces pressure into the US session.

A Nikkei rebound would be the first sign that the pressure on growth is easing.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1 of 10 and the VIX Spike tier at 2 of 4 describe different things, so they can coexist. The Crash Index reads price damage that has already happened, and today there is almost none.

The VIX Spike Detector reads what options traders expect next, and it shows a 60% probability with skew and backwardation both active. Skew means traders pay extra for downside puts.

Backwardation means near-term volatility costs more than later volatility, a sign of short-fuse worry. Calm price with priced-in fear is a coherent state: buyers of protection act before sellers of stock do.

Trust the VIX read for direction, and trust the Crash Index to confirm only if damage shows up. If the spike tier rises to 3, the gap closes from the options side first.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

How to read

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
